title: What does Japan's AI Promotion Act require of businesses?
seoTitle: Japan AI Promotion Act: business duties
description: Japan's AI Promotion Act (Act No. 53 of 2025), fully in force since September 1, 2025: what it asks of businesses, the AI Basic Plan and the guideline.
shortAnswer: Japan's Act on Promotion of Research and Development, and Utilization of Artificial Intelligence-related Technology (Act No. 53 of 2025) is a framework law, fully in force since September 1, 2025. Businesses that develop, provide or use AI must endeavor to use it actively and must cooperate with government measures, but the Act sets no specific compliance, reporting or training duties and no penalties. Practical expectations come from a voluntary guideline and the AI Basic Plan.
keyTakeaways: The Act was promulgated and partly brought into force on June 4, 2025; the provisions establishing the AI Basic Plan and the Artificial Intelligence Strategic Headquarters took effect on September 1, 2025.

Article 7 defines "utilization business operators" broadly, as anyone who develops or provides AI products or services or uses AI in business activities. The Cabinet Office guideline says this includes overseas business operators.
The business duties are general: endeavor to use AI to improve efficiency and create industries, and cooperate with national and local measures. There are no sanctions.

The Guideline for Ensuring the Appropriateness, decided December 19, 2025 under Article 13, lists five matters for businesses, including AI governance that covers education and training. It is voluntary.

The second AI Basic Plan, adopted by Cabinet decision on July 14, 2026, assigns the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare work on working styles in the AI era and supports reskilling for employees and workers.
regulator: Artificial Intelligence Strategic Headquarters, established under the Cabinet and chaired by the Prime Minister; affairs handled by the Cabinet Office
appliesTo: Utilization business operators: any person developing or providing products or services that use AI, or using AI in business activities, including overseas business operators
Research and development institutes, including universities (Article 6)
National and local governments, which carry most of the Act's concrete duties

sections.heading: What kind of law is the AI Promotion Act?

blocks.text: It is a framework law that sets principles, assigns responsibilities and creates government machinery, rather than a regulatory code with licensing, prohibitions or fines. The [Cabinet Office](https://www8.cao.go.jp/cstp/ai/ai_act/ai_act.html), which calls it the AI Act (AI hō), describes its aim as promoting AI innovation while responding to risks, and records that it was promulgated and partly brought into force on June 4, 2025, then fully in force on September 1, 2025.

The [English translation](https://www.japaneselawtranslation.go.jp/en/laws/view/5066/en) shows a compact structure: Chapter I general provisions (Articles 1 to 10), Chapter II basic measures (Articles 11 to 17), Chapter III the AI Basic Plan (Article 18), Chapter IV the AI Strategic Headquarters (Articles 19 to 28) and supplementary provisions. The [Japanese text on e-Gov](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/507AC0000000053) is authoritative. The Cabinet Office AI Act page, checked as at November 2026, links the original text and lists no amending act.

Article 2 defines "artificial intelligence-related technology" as technology needed to realize, by artificial means, functions that substitute for human cognition, inference and judgment, and the information processing systems that use it. Article 3(4) is the main risk clause: because AI used for wrong purposes or by inappropriate methods may facilitate crime, leaks of personal information, copyright infringement and other harms, measures such as ensuring transparency "must be implemented".

sections.heading: What must businesses do under the Act?

blocks.text: Very little that is specific. Article 7 is the only provision aimed at businesses, and it contains two duties with different force. A utilization business operator "is to endeavor" to raise efficiency and create new industries through active use of AI, and "must cooperate" with measures taken by national and local governments under Articles 4 and 5.

The cooperation duty has no defined content, no reporting obligation and no sanction. The Act contains no penalty provisions at all. A business's main direct touchpoint is Article 16, under which the national government analyzes cases where citizens' rights and interests are infringed by AI used for wrongful purposes or by inappropriate methods, and then gives "guidance, advice" and information to businesses, or takes other necessary measures. Guidance under Article 16 is not an order, but a business named in a case study or approached for information will want to show what governance it had in place.
Article 25(2) also lets the Headquarters ask for necessary cooperation from persons other than public bodies when it finds it particularly necessary. That is a request power, not a power to compel.

blocks.title: Is there a training duty?
blocks.text: No. The Act imposes no training or competence requirement on businesses. Article 14 (securing human resources) and Article 15 (promoting education) are duties of the national government. The literacy expectations for businesses come from soft law, covered on the page on [Japan's AI Guidelines for Business](/regulations/japan-ai-guidelines-for-business-training).

sections.heading: Who counts as a utilization business operator?

blocks.text: Almost every organization that uses AI. Article 7 covers any person who intends to develop or provide products or services using AI, and any other person who intends to use AI in business activities. An employer using a generative AI assistant, a recruitment screening tool or an AI scheduling system is a utilization business operator.

The Act does not state its territorial reach. The [Guideline for Ensuring the Appropriateness of Research and Development and Utilization of AI-related Technology](https://www8.cao.go.jp/cstp/ai/ai_guideline/ai_gl_eng_20260116.pdf) states, in a footnote to Section 2, that the utilization business operator defined in Article 7 includes overseas business operators. Foreign companies serving the Japanese market should therefore treat the guideline's expectations as addressed to them as well.

sections.heading: What does the appropriateness guideline expect from businesses?

blocks.text: The guideline, decided by the AI Strategic Headquarters on December 19, 2025 under Article 13, aims to "encourage voluntary and proactive efforts" and asks each stakeholder to respond at a suitable level for its scale, position and the risks of its AI. Section 2 lists five matters for research institutes and utilization business operators. The table maps them to the business roles and evidence that would show a voluntary effort if a ministry asked (original mapping).

blocks.text: Two details are directly relevant to employers. Footnote 18 says the information supplied with AI should include warnings to prevent inappropriate user behavior that could lead to unfair bias or discrimination "in hiring, performance evaluations, etc." And the guideline points to ISO/IEC 42001 and the Hiroshima AI Process reporting framework as ways to run a management system; see [ISO/IEC 42001 competence and awareness](/regulations/iso-iec-42001-competence-and-awareness).

sections.heading: What do the AI Basic Plan and the Strategic Headquarters do?

blocks.text: The Headquarters drafts and drives the AI Basic Plan, and the Plan sets government measures; neither imposes duties on businesses. Under Article 18 the Prime Minister seeks a Cabinet decision on a draft plan prepared by the Headquarters and publishes it without delay. Under Articles 19 to 24 the Headquarters sits under the Cabinet, is chaired by the Prime Minister, has the Chief Cabinet Secretary and the Minister for Artificial Intelligence Strategy as deputy chairs, and includes all other Ministers of State.

According to the [Cabinet Office AI Basic Plan page](https://www8.cao.go.jp/cstp/ai/ai_plan/ai_plan.html), the first plan was adopted by Cabinet decision on December 23, 2025 and the second, current plan on July 14, 2026. The [second plan](https://www8.cao.go.jp/cstp/ai/ai_plan/aiplan_eng_20260714.pdf) sets four principles (promoting innovation while mitigating risks; trial, learning and iteration; agile response; integrated domestic and international policy) and four strategic pillars, from accelerating AI deployment to building a society where humans and AI collaborate.

For workforce planning, the second plan flags concerns about agentic AI's impact on "ways of working and employment", lists support for "AI reskilling initiatives for individual employees and workers" with the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare among the responsible ministries, and assigns that ministry the lead on examining working styles suited to the AI era. These are government programs, but they signal where future guidance on employers is most likely to come from.

sections.heading: What should staff understand if the law requires no training?

blocks.text: Staff need enough understanding to make the organization's voluntary governance real, because that is what a ministry using Article 16 guidance powers, a business partner or a regulator under another law will ask about. In Japan, the binding obligations that touch AI in practice sit in other laws, such as the Act on the Protection of Personal Information; see [APPI employee training](/regulations/japan-appi-employee-training).

items: **Managers and AI governance owners:** the Article 7 cooperation duty, the five guideline matters, and how the organization records its voluntary measures.
**HR and people managers:** the guideline's warning about bias in hiring and performance evaluations, and how to question AI outputs before relying on them.
**Product and engineering teams:** transparency information users must receive, testing for misuse and hallucination, and provenance tools.
**All staff using AI:** the organization's acceptable use rules, data entry limits, and how to report a suspected rights infringement or incident.

blocks.text: Mapping each group to outcomes and evidence in a [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) gives a defensible record even where the law sets no minimum. For multinational employers, the comparison in [AI literacy and AI governance training by country](/compare/ai-literacy-and-ai-governance-training-by-country) shows how Japan's soft law approach differs from the binding duties in the EU.

It could, and the Act anticipates review. Article 2 of the Supplementary Provisions requires the government to review how the Act is operating, taking into account international policy trends and social and economic change, and to take required measures based on the results. The second Basic Plan also asks the Headquarters to aggregate information on technology trends and risk incidents and to encourage ministries to review AI-related systems, guidelines and measures, "including the AI Act". As at November 2026, no amending bill has been announced on the Cabinet Office AI pages.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records soft law expectations, such as the five guideline matters, in the same obligation structure as binding duties, marked as voluntary and linked to their source. Organizations can then show which measures they adopted, for which roles, and why, without overstating them as legal requirements.

faqs.q: Are there penalties for breaching Japan's AI Promotion Act?
faqs.a: No. The Act contains no penalty provisions. Its business duties are to endeavor to use AI actively and to cooperate with government measures. The national government may analyze rights infringement cases and give businesses guidance, advice and information under Article 16, which are not enforceable orders.

faqs.q: Does the Act apply to foreign companies?
faqs.a: The Act does not state territorial scope, but the Cabinet Office's appropriateness guideline says utilization business operators include overseas business operators. A foreign company providing AI products or services in Japan should assume the guideline's voluntary expectations are addressed to it.

faqs.q: How is the AI Promotion Act different from the AI Guidelines for Business?
faqs.a: The Act is legislation that sets principles, government duties and the Strategic Headquarters. The AI Guidelines for Business are non-binding guidance from the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications and the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry. The appropriateness guideline made under Article 13 sits between them as the Headquarters' own voluntary guideline.

faqs.q: Does the Act regulate AI used in hiring?
faqs.a: Not specifically. It has no employment provisions. The appropriateness guideline asks AI providers to warn users against behavior that could cause unfair bias in hiring and performance evaluations, and existing employment and personal information laws continue to apply to AI used in HR.

factCheck.claim: Cabinet Office page: AI Act promulgated and partly in force June 4, 2025 (Reiwa 7); fully in force September 1, 2025 including provisions establishing the AI Strategic Headquarters.

English translation, Act No. 53 of June 4, 2025: chapter structure; Article 2 definition; Article 3(4) transparency and other measures must be implemented; Article 7 utilization business operators 'is to endeavor' and 'must cooperate'; Articles 14 and 15 national government duties; Article 16 analysis of infringement cases and guidance, advice and information to businesses; Article 18 Basic Plan by Cabinet decision on Headquarters draft; Articles 19 to 24 Headquarters composition (Prime Minister chair; Chief Cabinet Secretary and Minister for AI Strategy deputy chairs; all other Ministers members); Article 25(2) cooperation requests; Supplementary Provisions Article 1 phased effect within three months, Article 2 review.
e-Gov holds the authoritative Japanese text of Act No. 53 of 2025 and it contains no penalty provisions (as recorded on the sibling AI Guidelines for Business page).

Appropriateness guideline decided December 19, 2025 under Article 13; aims to encourage voluntary and proactive efforts; respond at suitable level by scale, position and risks; Section 2 five matters (AI governance incl. implementation of education and training; transparency; safety; business continuity plan; data stakeholders); footnote 10 utilization business operator includes overseas business operators; footnote 12 and 16 refer to ISO/IEC 42001 and Hiroshima AI Process Reporting Framework; footnote 18 warnings to prevent unfair bias or discrimination in hiring, performance evaluations.
AI Basic Plan page: current plan Cabinet decision Reiwa 8 July 14 (2026); previous plan Cabinet decision Reiwa 7 December 23 (2025).

Second AI Basic Plan (as of July 14, 2026): four principles and four strategic pillars; concerns over agentic AI impact on ways of working and employment; measure (3)(iv) support AI reskilling initiatives for individual employees and workers (Cabinet Office lead; MEXT, MHLW, METI); MHLW lead on examining working styles appropriate for the AI era; mechanism to encourage ministries to review AI-related systems, guidelines and measures including the AI Act.
